Subject: Aurora Health - proposed benchmark/exclusivity guardrails (review requested)

Laura / Ben —

Quick summary: Aurora is ready to sign if we accept two non-standard commercial asks that Legal & Deal Desk flagged as high-risk: (1) a rolling benchmark protection that locks us to matching any benchmark price offered to their peers for 12 months, and (2) a limited exclusivity carve (they want us to agree not to sell to other regional providers in three named markets for the first 9 months of the contract).

They positioned these as deal-breakers given procurement and their board priorities. I pushed for narrower language and trade-offs (shorter duration, metrics-based benchmark trigger, carveouts for existing customers) — they sent redlines attached.

Request: can you review the attached SOW redlines and the benchmark appendix (both attached) and advise (a) what acceptable guardrails look like from Risk/Legal, (b) whether we can offer a pricing floor/offset to compensate, and (c) whether this requires an exec-level exception.

Context: ARR ~$3.1M first year, expansion upside in org-wide pilot. Aurora is a strong reference for our healthcare vertical and has strict SSO/HIPAA requirements (we already cleared security).

Attachments: Aurora_SOW_v3_redlines.pdf (redline), benchmark-definition-appendix.docx

Thanks — Vivek

--

Subject: Re: Aurora Health - proposed benchmark/exclusivity guardrails (review requested)

Vivek —

Thanks for flagging and for the clear summary. I skimmed the redlines and have a few initial points:

- Benchmark clause: the current language is open-ended and would require us to match any bona fide written offer to a similar buyer for 12 months. That is high-risk — very difficult to operationalize and creates recurring price-matching obligations. We should limit this to (i) offers that are demonstrably for the same scope (same modules, user counts, and support levels), (ii) a narrow look-back window (90 days), and (iii) require Aurora to provide written evidence and a price-reduction notification period (30 days) before any match obligation.

- Exclusivity: a regional exclusivity for named markets is more acceptable if it is (i) short (90 days), (ii) limited to the Pilot product only (not all Redwood products), and (iii) subject to carveouts for existing deals and for any customers under active negotiation we already have in pipeline. We should explicitly exclude marquee public-sector customers and reference customers.

- Remedies / caps: any pricing remedy should be capped (both $ and time) and accompanied by a termination right for Redwood if the match would cause material commercial harm.

I recommend we propose a counter that replaces 12 months with 90 days for benchmark matching, adds strict scope and evidence requirements, and pushes exclusivity to a 90-day market-limited pilot carve. If Sales wants additional commercial sweeteners, propose a one-time professional services credit (not an ongoing rebate).

If Ben confirms operational implications (billing/tracking) are manageable and Rishi agrees that this is within tolerable executive risk given ARR and reference value, we can draft proposed redlines to send to Aurora Contracts.

Laura

Subject: Re: Aurora Health - proposed benchmark/exclusivity guardrails (review requested)

Thanks Vivek / Laura —

Operational notes:
- Tracking: we can implement a very lightweight tracking flow for benchmark evidence (ingest Aurora-supplied docs into a secured contract folder + manual review). Not ideal long-term but workable for a short, capped period.
- Billing: to avoid open-ended rebates, finance wants any offset to be a one-time credit tied to a milestone (e.g., completion of pilot + adoption threshold). Ongoing price matching is high operational friction.
- Quantification: worst-case retention risk if we accept 12 months open MFN is ~7-9% revenue leakage annually for the cohort; limiting to 90 days drops that materially.

I'm comfortable with Laura's counter. If Sales insists on a longer term, we should require a stronger offset (larger upfront PS credit + strict scope).

-Ben

Subject: Fwd: Aurora Health - proposed benchmark/exclusivity guardrails (counterproposal)

Elaine / Samir —

Thanks for the quick turn on redlines. Per internal review, the earliest we can go on the benchmark/exclusivity asks is with the following guardrails: 

1) Benchmark match limited to pricing offers that are for the same product scope and support tier, with evidence required and a 30-day notice. Duration: 90 days from signature (not 12 months).
2) Exclusivity narrowed to the Pilot package only, and limited to three named markets for 90 days; carveouts for existing customers and publicly announced reference accounts.
3) Any commercial offset will be a one-time PS credit tied to Pilot completion (we propose $75k credit) rather than an ongoing rebate.

If Aurora can accept that language, we will prepare redlines for contracts to finalize. If they need longer protection, we need to escalate for exec approval and discuss a larger commercial offset.

Please advise — Vivek

Attachments: Aurora_SOW_v3_redlines.pdf (for reference)

Team / Elaine —

Thanks for the diligence and the revised proposal. From an exec perspective: Aurora is a strategic healthcare reference and 3.1M ARR is meaningful, but we cannot accept open-ended MFN-like language. Approve the Laura/Ben counter as the default path. Approvals: I authorize the 90-day benchmark window + 90-day pilot exclusivity with the one-time $75k PS credit proposed, provided the contract contains the explicit scope/evidence requirements and a cap on total remediation liability tied to the Pilot value.

If Aurora insists on 12 months or broader product exclusivity, escalate back to me with a full P&L impact (expected revenue leakage / credit sizing) and a suggested alternative (e.g., larger upfront discount in lieu of ongoing match).

Rishi
